text:
Linus Karlsson is the kind of player whose box score fibs. He has 10 points in 20 games and only three in his last ten, yet Thomas Drance named him the Canucks' top skater and a Daily Hive headline called him "an underrated beast." Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis described his part in a tying goal in Edmonton, with no point to show for it: a "Big reverse hit on Nugent-Hopkins to hold possession, great zone entry," then the cross-ice pass that opened it up.

The underlying case holds. Evolving-Hockey had him driving play last season (his team created 0.17 more expected goals per 60 with him on, 86th percentile among forwards) while skating with teammates in the bottom 3%. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found him getting to the home-plate area in front of the net for 6.7 chances per 60, 88th percentile. This season his finishing is right on his chances (four goals on 4.2 expected). He's a 2018 third-round pick of the Sharks who came up through Abbotsford, and on a team that has lost nine of ten, he keeps doing the work that doesn't always show.
headline: Linus Karlsson does the work the box score misses
